decisions.why: The DO Latin prints a comma: 'tu es, Deus' can be 'you are, O God' (you exist before the mountains) or 'you are God' (DRB, MS1932). The Rahlfs Greek in the parallels ends at σὺ εἶ, 'you are', which favours the absolute sense. The draft copies the Latin's comma and the bare vocative (as the finished psalms have it, D44): the ear takes the vocative first but the predicate can still be heard. The bare predicate would close the question the other way.

decisions.latin: tránseat, flóreat, tránseat … décidat, indúret, aréscat
decisions.why: Six subjunctives (the Greek has optatives: παρέλθοι, ἀνθήσαι, ἀποπέσοι, σκληρυνθείη, ξηρανθείη) with no named subject — man of 89:3, or the years of 89:5. DRB turns them into futures, MS1932 into presents; both resolve the mood. The draft keeps the bare subjunctive and leaves the subject unnamed, as the Latin does: it can be heard as a wish or as 'let it be so'. aréscere → secar, décidere → cair (as 36:2); herba → erva.

decisions.why: sǽculum here is a lifetime or an age (αἰών ἡμῶν), set in the light of God's face beside 'our iniquities'. decisions.why: The crux of the psalm. meditabúntur is a deponent future with the years as subject; L&S gives meditor a passive sense in late Latin ('considered, weighed'), and DRB ('shall be considered as a spider') and MS1932 ('serão considerados') both read it so. The Greek ἐμελέτων has the years as object (someone 'was pondering our years like a spider'). The draft follows the two Vulgate witnesses with 'considerados', the plainer of two faithful words (L&S 'consider'); the glossary's 'meditar' (row, working) would keep the verb one through the psalter but 'serão meditados' is not heard as Portuguese. MS1932's 'teia de' is his gloss and is not taken: the Latin names the spider.

decisions.why: novit governs both halves: who knows the power of your wrath, and (knows how) to count your wrath for fear of you. decisions.why: deprecábilis: 'that may be entreated, exorable' (L&S, citing this verse); the Greek παρακλήθητι is 'relent, be comforted'. decisions.latin: dírige fílios eórum … ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige … opus mánuum nostrárum dírige
decisions.why: Three dírige in two verses; one verb for the three keeps the Latin's repetition. The glossary row (open) gives 'endireitai' for dirígere at the vós imperative ('dirigi' = 'I directed') and names 89:16–17; with persons as object it leaves the psalm to decide ('encaminhai' a candidate). 'Endireitai os seus filhos' is heard as setting children right — correcting them — so the draft takes 'encaminhai' for all three. The Greek differs (ὁδήγησον in 16, κατεύθυνον in 17), but the Latin is one word and it is translated. 'guiai' is dedúcere's (D22).

choices.89:1: a generatióne in generatiónem → 'de geração em geração', the formula row's words (In generatiónem et generatiónem).
choices.89:2: orbis beside terra → 'a terra e o mundo' (D30 names 89:2). a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum → 'desde sempre e para todo o sempre' (40:14, D37, D41; the row says 89:2 should copy it). fíerent / formarétur → 'se fizessem / se formassem', the passive as reflexive and the verb before its subjects, to keep the first colon near the Latin's length (checks flagged +5 on 'fossem feitos … fossem formados'); the plural verb for terra et orbis is agreement, grammar.
choices.89:3: Convertímini said to men → 'Convertei-vos' (D25's exception for convértere; safe at the vós imperative with the enclitic, D13). fílii hóminum → 'filhos dos homens' (4:3). 'e dissestes' keeps the Latin's et.
choices.89:4: ante óculos tuos → 'diante dos vossos olhos' (as 13:3d / 35:2b). The copula 'são' supplied (D2). The verse ends on a comma and runs into 89:5, as the Latin does.
choices.89:6: The subject of the six verbs is left unnamed, as in the Latin; DRB supplies 'man'.
choices.89:7: Quia → 'Porque'; defícere → desfalecer (row); ira / furor → ira / furor (row).
choices.89:8: in conspéctu tuo → 'à vossa vista' (row; 55:9's versicle 'Pusestes as minhas lágrimas à vossa vista' is the same build). vultus → rosto (row).
choices.89:9b: in ipsis → 'neles', moved to the head of the colon; 'são' supplied. aránea → 'a aranha', with the article, as a kind.
choices.89:10: labor et dolor → 'fadiga e dor' (row, 9:28). 'é' supplied.
choices.89:10b: mansuetúdo → 'mansidão' (row, noun of manso); corrípere → castigar (D21; the row names 89:10). The sense of the verse (mildness came, and we shall be chastened) is the Latin's own puzzle and is not explained.
choices.89:11: novit → 'conhece' (perfect with present sense). potéstas → 'poder'. The Latin's iræ tuæ … iram tuam is kept twice.
choices.89:12: notam fac → 'fazei conhecer' (row, 76:15 'Fizestes conhecer'). erudíti → 'instruídos' (erudíre → instruir, row); the Latin follows the reading πεπαιδευμένους, not Rahlfs' πεπεδημένους 'fettered', and the Latin is followed. The second colon is a second object of 'fazei conhecer', verbless as in the Latin.
choices.89:14: exsultáre → exultar; delectári → deleitar-se (D44). ómnibus diébus nostris → 'em todos os nossos dias'. The Portuguese -amos forms are past and present at once; the context (repléti sumus) gives the past.
choices.89:15: pro → 'pelos'; the bare ablative annis takes the same 'pelos' (grammar). mala → 'males' (row).
choices.89:16: Réspice in → 'Olhai para' (formula, 68:17, 73:20). ópera tua → 'as vossas obras'; 'seus filhos' = the servants' sons.
choices.89:17: splendor → 'esplendor' (λαμπρότης). sit → 'esteja' (jussive). 'sobre nós' twice, as the Latin. The last colon keeps the Latin's plain 'et' (MS1932's 'sim' is emphasis the Latin does not have). ópera (plural) and opus (singular) keep their numbers.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the parallels, glossary and DECISIONS. Hard readings: 89:9b aránea … meditabúntur; 89:10 potentátibus and ámplius eórum; 89:13 deprecábilis; 89:6's six subjunctives; 89:16–17 dírige against the glossary's endireitai.

Hard checks pass. Soft flags accepted: 89:1 second colon −6 (the formula 'de geração em geração'); 89:8 second colon −5 (the Latin's long illuminatióne against 'luz', row); 89:9b first colon +3 ('considerados'); 89:10 first colon −3; 89:12 +4 / +3 (the Latin's terse 'notam fac' and 'erudítos corde' need Portuguese periphrasis); the rhymes ira / ira (89:11) and mãos / mãos (89:17) are the Latin's own repetitions. 89:2 first colon was +5 and was shortened with reflexive passives to +4 (the counter does not elide; with sinalefa it is about +2), accepted.
